question: Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act was enacted in which year?
solution:
The correct answer is __**2003**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) Act** was enacted in the year **2003** to institutionalize financial discipline and reduce India's fiscal deficit.
 
• The Act was introduced by the **Government of India** under the leadership of then Finance Minister **Jaswant Singh** during the **Atal Bihari Vajpayee**-led NDA government.
 
• The primary objective of the Act was to ensure **long-term macroeconomic stability**, better coordination between monetary and fiscal policy, and greater transparency in India’s fiscal management system.
 
• The FRBM Act sets **quantitative fiscal targets** such as reducing the fiscal deficit to a certain percentage of GDP and eliminating revenue deficit by a stipulated time.
 
• The Act promotes accountability by requiring the government to present an annual **Medium-Term Fiscal Policy Statement**, **Fiscal Policy Strategy Statement**, and **Macroeconomic Framework Statement** to Parliament.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Significance of the FRBM Act:**

 
 
• The Act was aimed at improving **fiscal prudence** by reducing India's mounting fiscal and revenue deficits.
 
• It mandated the government to limit the fiscal deficit to **3% of GDP** and eliminate the revenue deficit by 2008-09. However, this deadline was later extended due to economic challenges, including the global financial crisis of 2008.
 
• It enhances **transparency** and ensures that the government follows a disciplined approach to fiscal management by requiring regular updates and disclosure of fiscal data.
 
 
 
• **Amendments to the FRBM Act:**
 
 
• The Act has undergone amendments over time to accommodate changing economic needs. For instance, in **2018**, a new fiscal target was introduced under the **FRBM (Amendment) Act**, requiring the government to keep the fiscal deficit below **3.1% of GDP** by 2020-21.
 
• It also introduced the concept of a **debt-to-GDP ratio**, mandating the central government to reduce its debt to **40%** of GDP by 2024-25.
 
 
 
• **Exemptions under the FRBM Act:**
 
 
• The Act allows exemptions in case of **national security concerns, natural calamities, or other exceptional circumstances** that require higher government spending.
 
• For example, during the **COVID-19 pandemic**, the government invoked these exemptions to accommodate increased fiscal spending to manage the crisis.
 
 
 
• **Fiscal Terms Defined:**
 
 
• **Fiscal Deficit:** The difference between the government’s total expenditure and its total revenue (excluding borrowings).
 
• **Revenue Deficit:** The gap between the government's revenue receipts and revenue expenditures.
 
• **Primary Deficit:** The fiscal deficit minus interest payments on past borrowings.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The FRBM Act is often compared to similar legislation in other countries, such as the **Gramm-Rudman-Hollings Act** in the United States, which also aimed to control fiscal deficits.
 
• The **14th Finance Commission** recommended a review of the FRBM Act to make it more flexible and adaptable to changing economic scenarios.
 
• The **NK Singh Committee**, formed in 2016, suggested several reforms to the FRBM Act, including the adoption of a **debt-to-GDP target** and a more realistic fiscal deficit target.
 
• The Act has been a cornerstone of India’s fiscal policy, influencing budgetary decisions and long-term economic planning.
